title: EXEC SQL ... :WS-FIELD — host variable binding; precompiler turns it into a parameter call
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. UPDATE-BALANCE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-ACCT-ID    PIC X(10).
       01  WS-NEW-BAL    PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
       01  SQLCODE       PIC S9(9) COMP.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> The DB2 precompiler scans for EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC blocks
      *> and rewrites them as CALL invocations to the runtime, with
      *> host variables (colon-prefixed) mapped to bind parameters.
      *> SQLCODE is a magic COMPILER-injected status. A Java/JDBC
      *> port uses PreparedStatement + setObject(); the spec must
      *> capture each host variable's PIC.
           EXEC SQL
              UPDATE ACCOUNTS SET BALANCE = :WS-NEW-BAL
              WHERE ACCT_ID = :WS-ACCT-ID
           END-EXEC.
notes: EXEC SQL is the legacy DB2 binding. The precompiler is the bridge — modern rewrites use JDBC PreparedStatement. The spec must list every host variable + its PIC so the rewrite's parameter types are correct.
